body:
I have raised the problem of the previous issue.https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/issues/842
Should this license and the previous license both be given distinguished names?
![license-webm-patent-cross-nvdia](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2231549/55669353-3d280780-58b1-11e9-9d17-860a0208288a.png)

This license is similar to the license that is called as NVDIA-r2 or NVDIA-EULA in caluclate-linux or scanCode-toolKit.

The URL provided in the request (https://www.webmproject.org/cross-license/vp8/agreement/) appears to be a bilateral patent cross-licensing agreement. I don't see this as an open source license and/or something that would fall within the general bounds of the [SPDX license inclusion principles](https://spdx.org/spdx-license-list/license-list-overview).

I suggest closing the issue and not including this on the license list.
I am satisfied that I confirmed that this license is different from "spdx/Google patent grant" #646.

I've reviewed the license language and agree that it is not an open-source license, nor is it similar enough to open-source (or even source-available) to justify inclusion on the SPDX License List.

First, it is a cross-license, not a one-way grant:

> Because Google is offering this license to You for free, as a condition of granting the license, Google requires that You grant back to Google, to the Primary Licensors and to all others who enter into the VP8 Patent Cross-License Agreement, a free and worldwide license under any patent(s) You or Your Affiliates, if any, own or can freely license that are necessary for the implementation of the VP8 Format.
> ...
> Subject to the terms and conditions of this VP8 Patent Cross-License Agreement, You, on behalf of Yourself and Your Affiliates (if any), grant to the Primary Licensors, to Google and its Affiliates, to each of their respective direct and indirect vendors, suppliers, licensors, contractors, resellers, distributors, customers, licensees, lessees and end users, in their capacity as such, and to all other VP8 Licensees (all of the foregoing, the "Reciprocal Licensees"): (i) a non-assignable and non-transferrable, non-sublicenseable, worldwide, royalty-free, nonexclusive license to Exploit Licensed Products in the Licensed Field of Use under those patent claims, if any, now or hereafter owned or licensable by You or Your Affiliates that must necessarily be infringed by the act of Exploiting Licensed Products in the Licensed Field of Use, and (ii) a worldwide, royalty-free release from any claims of infringement for any prior activities that would have been licensed hereunder had those activities occurred on or after the date You entered into this VP8 Patent Cross-License Agreement.


Second, it requires explicit written agreement in one of the specified forms:
> You must express Your agreement in one of two ways: (i) by clicking on the button at the end of this document and providing all of the required information; or (ii) by signing a paper copy of this agreement (the printable form is available here) and sending the signed original VP8 Patent Cross-License Agreement to:
>
> Patent Licensing Team
> 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway
> Mountain View, CA 94043
>
> Signed agreements may also be scanned and emailed in PDF form to patentlicensing@google.com with the following email subject line: "VP8 Patent Cross-License Agreement - [Your name]". "[Your name]" can be your corporate/organization name or your individual name, depending on who is entering into this Agreement.

Third, the license is explicitly not sublicenseable:
> Subject to the terms and conditions of this VP8 Patent Cross-License Agreement, Google grants to You a non-assignable and non-transferrable, non-sublicenseable, worldwide, royalty-free, nonexclusive license [...]


Fourth, the WebM VP8 cross-license does not require making source available, nor indeed address copyright in source code at all. 


Although SPDX does consider "open-source-like" patent license grants for inclusion in the SPDX License List (indeed we intend to add a Google patent grant in #646 to the Exceptions List), the factors above, when considered together, preclude adding this to the SPDX License List. I think this license should not be included and this issue be closed.

To be clear, I would not foreclose the possibility that the WebM VP8 license may be a good candidate for inclusion in [proposed private namespaces](https://github.com/nexB/spdx-license-namespaces-registry/) using the SPDX spec; it would probably be a good candidate. Nevertheless it is not suitable for the main SPDX License List.

agree with @swinslow and @bradleeedmondson analysis here on not adding. adding label and closing as a result. 

you can also always use LicenseRef as per section 6 of the SPDX spec https://spdx.org/spdx-specification-21-web-version#h.1v1yuxt
